newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding, but only if Fed funds tighten up.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding, but only if Fed funds tighten up.

text.p: A still high add need should push the Federal Reserve to inject reserves into the banking system Tuesday, but the soft level of federal funds may keep the Fed on the sidelines for another day, analysts said.
Two-day system repurchase agreements would be most likely.
Fed funds opened at 5-3/16 percent, below the 5-1/4 percent target rate.

"I was surprised at the softness in funds yesterday," said Kathy Bostjancic, money market analyst at UBS Securities Inc. Funds fell as low as 4-7/8 percent Monday before climbing to close at 5-1/4 percent.

"If funds are soft close to intervention time I would expect the Fed to pass again today," Bostjancic said. "But if funds are close to target, they'll do two-day system RPs. Reserves still have a sizable add need."

She and others forecast a $5 billion to $6.5 billion add need for the remaining two days of the period. Should the Fed stay out of the open market today, a customer RPs or overnight system RPs would be required Wednesday.
Analysts are perplexed as to the little pressure on fed funds the past couple sessions.

"Since they were out of the market yesterday there's another factor supplying more reserves than expected," contended James Blumenthal, money market analyst at MCM MoneyWatch, adding that it is possible Friday's operation of weekend system RPs were larger than thought, "and the Fed has gotten ahead of its add job."
Meanwhile, analysts still look for a bill pass either Tuesday or Wednesday -- most likely Wednesday -- as the add need jumps next period.
